items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:24:1
items.html:
And this is what he says, “And behold, had AVI, etc. But since they receive only from the end of the Ozen, which is the place of the Shibolet of the beard, therefore, even though they take a little illumination, it does not avail them, and therefore the posterior of their vessels was broken.” For in truth they were included in the first coupling in the measure of the male, and then they too attained of the light of the level of phase two of the male; and if so, AVI too have the illumination of the Ozen just as the male has. But as was explained above, since they are in themselves only a record of phase one, this inclusion with the male is not reckoned for them as anything but the discernment of an illumination of the light of the Ozen, and not the self, as it is for the male. See above. And had they received this illumination “while they were near the place of the openings of the Ozen” — that is to say, had the AVI of Nekudim been the discernment of the female in the first Rosh [head] of the Dikna [beard], which are the two corrections called the hairs of the lip and the Orcha [path] — then certainly their posterior would not have been broken, like the first Rosh of the Nekudim, called YESHSUT, which endured in its entirety. But since they are the discernment of the second Rosh, which take only from the discernment of the Shibolet, and they do not have the self of the light of the Ozen but only an illumination alone, therefore their posterior was broken.
And this is what he says, “But the Keter, since it takes the light of the Ozen itself, even though it took it at its end, since it takes its self, this suffices, and not even its posterior was broken.” That is, as explained, that the Keter is the secret of the male, who has in himself the level of phase two, and therefore the light of the Ozen is reckoned as his self. And the matter of the difference between posterior and anterior will be explained in its place below.
And now you will understand still better the matter of the light of the Ozen that was blocked upon the Shibolet, brought in the words of the ARI above (page 411, item 21), and two reasons have already been explained there in the Inner Light. And with what is explained here concerning the male and female that are in the light of the Einayim — that even the male does not have phase two in her wholeness, but only half of this record, that is, only the discernment of clothing in her, for which reason there was no discernment of expansion in vessels from the first coupling that emerged in the level of Bina, as above (on page 412, the passage beginning “And from here”). Therefore, even after the second coupling, in the inclusion of the male in the female, when they descended and expanded to the Guf [body] — which are the external AHP, which in the Dikna [beard] are called the Shibolet, and in the Partzuf of Nekudim are the GAR [first three] of Nekudim — even then they cannot illuminate the light of Bina to the vessels below them, because of the lack of the discernment of the coarseness of drawing that there is in phase two, as above. Therefore the light of the Ozen was blocked in the Shibolet, which is the vessel of these ZON, for they cannot bestow of their light of Bina. And in this manner, in the GAR of Nekudim, the light of the Ozen was blocked in the Bina, and they cannot bestow anything outside themselves. And this matter was explained at length above (page 324, the passage beginning “And we should understand”). Study it there well. For here too (34) it is discerned that the light of Bina remained in the Rosh [head] beneath the Malchut of the Rosh, in the manner of the light of Keter with AB, and in the manner of the light of Hochma with SAG. Study it there well, for the whole matter from there applies here as well.
